payload.task_text:
You are a business development manager for TechStore Online, an e-commerce company selling consumer electronics and accessories. Your task is to plan a product roadshow in Shanghai and Guangzhou to meet regional distributors, selecting the right products to demonstrate based on store sales data, arranging train travel from Beijing, building a comprehensive roadshow plan spreadsheet, documenting the plan in the company knowledge base, and notifying all key contacts.

Start by analyzing the online store data. Retrieve the top ten products by sales volume from the product sales report. For each of the top five products, get the full product details including name, price, category, and stock status. Then retrieve the customer list and examine the billing location information to understand regional customer distribution. Also pull the orders report to understand regional revenue patterns. Per the company's strategic direction, the roadshow will focus on Shanghai and Guangzhou; use the customer and orders analysis to prepare the regional overview and mark Shanghai and Guangzhou as Priority 1 in the plan.

Next, plan the train travel. Look up the station codes for Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou using the train booking system. Query available high-speed trains from Beijing South station to Shanghai Hongqiao station on March 10, 2026, and from Beijing South to Guangzhou South on the same day. Review the options for each leg and pick one suitable for arriving in time for the afternoon meetings. The roadshow configuration file in your workspace lists the preferred trains for both legs; use those selections so the itinerary aligns with the company's standing travel preferences.

Create an Excel workbook named Roadshow_Plan.xlsx in your workspace. It must contain four sheets. The first sheet should be named Products and contain columns: Product_ID, Name, Category, Price_USD, Stock_Status, and Monthly_Sales_Est. Populate it with the five products selected for demonstration. The second sheet should be named Customer_Regions and contain columns: Region, Customer_Count, Revenue_Share_Pct, and Priority. Add rows for the key regions identified in the customer data analysis, marking Shanghai and Guangzhou as Priority 1. The third sheet should be named Travel_Itinerary and contain columns: Date, Train_No, From, To, Depart, Arrive, Duration_Hours, and Purpose. Add a row for the journey to Shanghai on March 10 and a row for the journey to Guangzhou. The fourth sheet should be named Roadshow_Schedule and contain columns: City, Date, Venue, Meeting_Type, Key_Contacts, and Status. Add at least four rows covering the Shanghai meeting on March 10 and the Guangzhou meeting on March 11. Write all numeric values (prices, counts, percentages, durations) as literal numbers in the cells; do not use spreadsheet formulas.

Create a page in the company knowledge base titled "Product Roadshow 2026 - Shanghai and Guangzhou". Add a section highlighting the five demonstration products with key selling points for each. Add a travel itinerary section showing both train journeys with departure and arrival details. Add a checklist section called "Follow-up Actions" listing items such as sending product catalogs to distributors, collecting distributor feedback forms, and scheduling follow-up calls.

Send an email to shanghai_dist@partner.com with subject "Roadshow Meeting Confirmation - Shanghai March 10" providing full details of the planned meeting time, venue, and products to be demonstrated. Send a second email to guangzhou_dist@partner.com with subject "Roadshow Meeting Confirmation - Guangzhou March 11" with the Guangzhou meeting details and a list of products. Send a summary email to manager@company.com with subject "Roadshow Plan Summary - Shanghai and Guangzhou March 2026" attaching a brief overview of the itinerary, the five products selected, and the expected business outcomes.

Configuration for this task is in roadshow_config.json and the planning methodology guide is in business_guide.md, both in your workspace.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use exactly one read-only source wave. Before dispatch, the main agent reads `roadshow_config.json` and `business_guide.md` and freezes the preferred train displays, two-city schedule, three exact email pairs, and output schemas.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): The WooCommerce explore sub-agent calls `woo_reports_top_sellers` once, retrieves the exact top-five products by ID with one `woo_products_get` call per ID, and fully paginates only `woo_customers_list` and `woo_orders_list` at `perPage=100`. Omit the optional order status field to request the unfiltered collection, aggregate every observed status locally, and return only the five product rows plus compact Shanghai/Guangzhou customer-count, order-revenue, share, page, and join controls. Do not write files or modify the store.
   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 0): The rail explore sub-agent resolves Beijing South, Shanghai Hongqiao, and Guangzhou South codes, queries both 2026-03-10 high-speed routes, and returns the exact task-configured preferred trains with display train number, route identifier where required, departure, arrival, duration, and first-class evidence. Do not write files.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates the two compact handoffs once and directly owns all outputs. Create `Roadshow_Plan.xlsx` with exactly the four required sheets, five products, both configured train rows, and at least four city schedule rows using literal numeric values. In an independent branch, exact-title search and create/update at most one `Product Roadshow 2026 - Shanghai and Guangzhou` page with the five product selling points, both train legs, and `Follow-up Actions`. Read the workbook and page once, then send at most one missing message for each of the three exact recipient/subject pairs. Do not dispatch a writer or verification wave.

nodes.text:
You are gathering read-only sales data from a WooCommerce store for TechStore Online (consumer electronics e-commerce). We are planning a distributor roadshow in Shanghai and Guangzhou and need store evidence. Do all work with the mcp__woocommerce__* tools.

Perform these steps:

1. TOP 10 PRODUCTS BY SALES VOLUME (the "product sales report"):
   - Call woo_reports_products (try with period "year"; if empty, try without period, or period "month"/"last_month"). It returns products with quantity sold. Also call woo_reports_top_sellers as a cross-check.
   - Record the top 10 products by sales volume/quantity, each with product_id, name, and quantity sold.

2. FULL DETAILS FOR THE TOP 5 PRODUCTS:
   - For each of the top 5 product IDs, call woo_products_get.
   - Record: id, name, type, category names, price (use price field, in USD as displayed), stock_status / stock_quantity / manage_stock, and any sold/total_sales meta fields.
   - Also note estimated monthly sales if derivable: use the products report figures: if the report is yearly use quantity/12 rounded to a whole number; if monthly use the reported quantity directly. State clearly how you derived it.

3. CUSTOMER LIST AND REGIONAL DISTRIBUTION:
   - Call woo_customers_list with perPage=100, paging through all customers.
   - For each customer extract billing address fields: city, state, country, postcode.
   - Aggregate customer counts by billing state/city (focus on China regions; if billing state is like "Shanghai"/"Guangdong"/"Beijing", use state; if state missing fall back to city).
   - Report total customer count and per-region counts.

4. ORDERS REPORT AND REGIONAL REVENUE:
   - Call woo_reports_orders with period "year" (fallback "month") and record totals: total_sales, total_orders, average order value, totals_per_period if present.
   - Then call woo_orders_list with perPage=100, paging through all orders, extracting each order's billing city/state and line_items totals. Aggregate revenue (order total) by billing region.
   - Compute each region's revenue share as percent of total order revenue (one decimal place).

5. PRIORITY ASSIGNMENT per company policy:
   - Revenue share > 20% => Priority 1; share 10-20% => Priority 2; otherwise Priority 3.
   - Per company strategic direction, Shanghai and Guangzhou MUST be Priority 1 regardless of computed share.
   - Produce a final Customer_Regions table: Region | Customer_Count | Revenue_Share_Pct | Priority, sorted descending by Revenue_Share_Pct. Include all regions that appear in either customers or orders data.

DELIVERABLE (return exactly this in your final message, clearly formatted):
A) TOP10: table of product_id, name, quantity_sold
B) TOP5_DETAILS: for each: product_id, name, category, price_usd (number), stock_status (e.g. "In Stock (N units)" or "Out of Stock"), monthly_sales_est (whole number), plus 1 short selling point from description if available
C) CUSTOMER_SUMMARY: total customers, region counts
D) ORDERS_SUMMARY: total_sales, total_orders, avg order value, any totals per period
E) CUSTOMER_REGIONS_FINAL: the final table with Region, Customer_Count, Revenue_Share_Pct, Priority
F) Notes: any data anomalies or assumptions you made.

Do not attempt to write anywhere. Read-only. If a tool errors, retry once with adjusted params, then report the error and continue with what you have.
WooCommerce roadshow data analysis

You are gathering read-only China rail data from the 12306 MCP tools for a business roadshow itinerary. Task: we need to travel from Beijing to Shanghai, and Beijing to Guangzhou, on 2026-03-10. Company policy pre-selects train G11 for Beijing→Shanghai and G105 for Beijing→Guangzhou; your job is to look up station codes and verify/retrieve these trains' schedule details.

Steps:
1. Call mcp__rail_12306__get-station-code-by-names with "北京南|上海虹桥|广州南" to get station codes and telecodes for Beijing South, Shanghai Hongqiao, Guangzhou South. (If a name fails, retry individually, e.g. "北京南", "上海虹桥", "广州南".)
2. Call mcp__rail_12306__get-current-date to know today's date in Shanghai timezone.
3. Call mcp__rail_12306__get-tickets with date "2026-03-10", fromStation = Beijing South station code, toStation = Shanghai Hongqiao station code, trainFilterFlags "G" (high-speed). Sort by startTime if supported. Find train G11 in the results.
4. Call mcp__rail_12306__get-tickets with date "2026-03-10", fromStation = Beijing South code, toStation = Guangzhou South code, trainFilterFlags "G". Find train G105.
5. IMPORTANT: if 2026-03-10 is outside the booking/sale window and a query returns empty or an error, note that fact, then re-run the same two queries using the closest available date (e.g. today's date or the latest queryable date) to recover the schedule times for G11 and G105, and clearly label which date returned the schedule.

For each of G11 and G105 record: train_no (the internal number like "2400000G11..."), departure station/time, arrival station/time, duration (历时, converted to decimal hours, e.g. 05:31 -> 5.52), and first-class (一等座) seat availability field if present.

DELIVERABLE (return exactly this):
A) STATION_CODES: Beijing South (name, station_code, telecode), Shanghai Hongqiao (same), Guangzhou South (same)
B) G11: date queried, departure station+time, arrival station+time, duration hours (decimal, 2 digits), first-class availability field value
C) G105: same fields
D) WINDOW_NOTE: whether 2026-03-10 was queryable; if substitute dates were used, state them.

Read-only task; do not book or modify anything. If a call errors, retry once, then report and continue.
12306 train schedule lookup

Create a Notion page in the company knowledge base. Use the mcp__notion__API-post-page tool.

Known environment issue: direct calls to API-post-page with parent {"workspace": true} or {"type":"workspace","workspace":true} or {"page_id":"..."} failed validation with errors like "/parent must be object ... must match exactly one schema in oneOf". That validation quirk may be serialization-specific to another caller. Try these parent variants in order until one passes validation:
1) {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true}
2) {"workspace": true}
3) If both fail, call mcp__notion__API-post-search (no args) to list visible pages/databases; if a page object is visible, use parent {"type": "page_id", "page_id": "<that page's id>"}. If none visible, try API-post-page once more with variant 1 (transient errors possible), then report the exact validation error text if all attempts fail.

PAGE TITLE (properties): title = "Product Roadshow 2026 - Shanghai and Guangzhou". Pass properties as {"title": {"title": [{"type": "text", "text": {"content": "Product Roadshow 2026 - Shanghai and Guangzhou"}}]}}.

PAGE CONTENT (children blocks, in this exact order — use standard Notion block JSON {"type": "...", "<type>": {"rich_text": [{"type":"text","text":{"content":"..."}}]}}):
1. paragraph: "TechStore Online is hosting a distributor roadshow in Shanghai (March 10-11, 2026) and Guangzhou (March 11-12, 2026). Shanghai and Guangzhou are designated Priority 1 regions per company strategic direction. The five demonstration products below were selected from the online store's top ten sellers by annual sales volume (source: WooCommerce sales report). A detailed plan is maintained in Roadshow_Plan.xlsx (sheets: Products, Customer_Regions, Travel_Itinerary, Roadshow_Schedule)."
2. heading_2: "Demonstration Products (Top 5 by Sales Volume)"
3. bulleted_list_item: "NIHARA Wood Smart Multipurpose Foldable Laptop Table with Cup Holder (Black) — $2.64, Electronics, ~17 units/month. Selling points: store #1 seller (199 units/year); foldable multipurpose design with integrated cup holder; ergonomic rounded edges; unbeatable entry price for volume distribution."
4. bulleted_list_item: "(Renewed) JBL Flip 4 Portable Wireless Speaker (Squad) — $86.72, Audio > Speakers, ~17 units/month. Selling points: iconic JBL audio with powerful bass; portable rugged build; built-in mic for calls; premium brand recognition drives retail pull-through."
5. bulleted_list_item: "LIMBANI BROTHERS™ Automatic Vacuum Sealing Machine — $12.04, Home Appliances, ~16 units/month. Selling points: fully automatic one-touch vacuum sealing for flatbreads, nuts, fruits and vegetables; strong value proposition at a low price point; ideal everyday home appliance."
6. bulleted_list_item: "Oraimo 25.5W 4-Port USB Wall Charger (5.1A) — $7.22, Electronics, ~16 units/month. Selling points: charges four devices simultaneously at 25.5W/5.1A total; compact travel size; wide compatibility including iPhone 13/12/Pro Max; essential mobile accessory with fast turnover."
7. bulleted_list_item: "Oppo Enco Air 3 True Wireless Earbuds (Glaze White) — $36.13, Audio > Headphones, ~16 units/month. Selling points: 25-hour total playtime with fast charging; large 13.4 mm drivers for rich sound; Bluetooth 5.3 stability; strong brand appeal in the TWS category."
8. heading_2: "Travel Itinerary"
9. bulleted_list_item: "March 10, 2026 — Train G11: Beijing South depart 07:00 → Shanghai Hongqiao arrive 12:31 (duration 5.52 hours), first class (¥933). Arrives ahead of the 14:00 Shanghai distributor meeting at Shanghai Pudong Conference Center."
10. bulleted_list_item: "March 10, 2026 — Train G105: Beijing South depart 08:00 → Guangzhou South arrive 15:48 (duration 7.80 hours), first class (¥1383). Arrives the evening before the March 11 Guangzhou distributor meeting at Guangzhou Tianhe Business Hotel Conference Center."
11. heading_2: "Meeting Schedule"
12. bulleted_list_item: "Shanghai — March 10, 2026, 14:00-16:00, Shanghai Pudong Conference Center: live demonstration of all five products plus commercial negotiation and distributor terms discussion. Key contact: shanghai_dist@partner.com."
13. bulleted_list_item: "Guangzhou — March 11, 2026, 09:00-11:00, Guangzhou Tianhe Business Hotel Conference Center: live demonstration of all five products plus commercial negotiation and distributor terms discussion. Key contact: guangzhou_dist@partner.com."
14. heading_2: "Follow-up Actions"
15. to_do (checked false): "Send product catalogs and specification sheets to Shanghai and Guangzhou distributors"
16. to_do (checked false): "Collect distributor feedback forms after each demonstration session"
17. to_do (checked false): "Schedule follow-up calls with both distributors (two weeks after the roadshow)"
18. to_do (checked false): "Send follow-up email with meeting notes and proposed distributor terms within 48 hours of each meeting"

If the children array causes validation issues, you may create the page with just title + first blocks, then append the remaining blocks with mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children using the new page id.

DELIVERABLE: report success/failure, the created page id and url if successful, or the exact error text from each attempt if all failed.
